source: Curated Paraphase medically relevant duplicated and difficult regions

regions.summary: Clinically relevant copy-number calls for SMN1, SMN2, and SMN exon 7-8 deletion alleles.
notes: A null SMN1 or SMN2 copy-number call can occur when Paraphase finds one haplotype but depth does not unambiguously support copy number one versus two.

clinical.interpretation: Read SMN1 copy number first: 0 copies = SMA-affected, 1 = carrier, 2 = normal. SMN2 copy number does not change affected/carrier status but modifies severity in affected people (more SMN2 = milder).
clinical.pathogenic: SMN1 CN 0 -> SMA-affected; report SMN2 CN as a severity modifier (fewer SMN2 = more severe).
clinical.caveats: Misses silent 2+0 carriers (appear as SMN1 CN 2) and intragenic point mutations in an otherwise-present SMN1.

regions.summary: Complex RCCX structural variation spanning CYP21A2, TNXB, and complement C4 genes.

field_descriptions.ending_hap: Final RCCX copy on each allele; only these copies contain TNXB rather than TNXA.
field_descriptions.starting_hap: First RCCX copy on each allele, used to infer RCCX haplotype order.
field_descriptions.deletion_hap: Deletion haplotype with both starting and ending characteristics, consistent with one RCCX copy on the allele.
field_descriptions.hap_variants: Common CYP21A2/CYP21A1P differentiating variants used for allele annotation.
field_descriptions.phasing_success: Whether RCCX haplotypes could be connected into alleles.
field_descriptions.annotated_alleles: Per-allele CYP21A2 annotations such as WT, pseudogene deletion, gene duplication, or fusion deletion alleles.

disorders.name: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome due to TNXB deficiency
Complement C4 variation and autoimmune disease susceptibility

clinical.interpretation: Read the per-allele CYP21A2/CYP21A1P annotation, not total copy number. 21-hydroxylase CAH is recessive: a damaging allele (CYP21A2 deletion, pseudogene-derived fusion/chimera, or pathogenic variant) on BOTH alleles = affected; one normal allele = carrier.
clinical.normal: Each allele has one functional CYP21A2 + one CYP21A1P (WT); isolated pseudogene duplication/deletion or a benign gene duplication are not disease.
clinical.carrier: One affected allele (CYP21A2 deletion, CYP21A1P/CYP21A2 fusion, or pathogenic variant) with a normal allele.
clinical.pathogenic: Biallelic damaging alleles (gene deletion, chimeric/30-kb deletion alleles, gene conversion, or known pathogenic CYP21A2 variants).
clinical.caveats: Allele-dependent, not inferable from copy number alone (e.g. a WT+Q319X duplication allele is NOT pathogenic).

regions.summary: PMS2 copy-number and haplotype resolution in a duplicated/pseudogene-rich Lynch syndrome region.

clinical.interpretation: Paraphase assigns 3' exon variants to the functional PMS2 gene vs the PMS2CL pseudogene. Lynch syndrome is dominant: a pathogenic variant in PMS2 (not PMS2CL) = predisposition; biallelic PMS2 variants cause CMMRD.
clinical.normal: Variant localized to the PMS2CL pseudogene, or no pathogenic PMS2 variant.
clinical.carrier: One pathogenic PMS2 variant = Lynch predisposition (dominant).
clinical.pathogenic: Pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variant assigned to functional PMS2 (including resolved 3'-exon variants).
clinical.caveats: Variant- and gene-assignment-dependent (PMS2 vs PMS2CL), not a copy-number call.

regions.summary: STRC copy-number changes are a common cause of hereditary hearing loss.

clinical.interpretation: STRC is recessive and Paraphase distinguishes it from its near-identical pseudogene: 2 functional copies = normal, 1 = carrier, 0 = biallelic loss consistent with DFNB16 hearing loss.
clinical.pathogenic: STRC CN 0 -> biallelic loss / DFNB16 hearing loss; a deletion extending into CATSPER2 causes deafness-infertility syndrome in males.
clinical.caveats: A single-copy deletion plus a point variant on the other allele also causes hearing loss, so CN 1 is not safely carrier-only.

regions.summary: IKBKG copy-number and rearrangement calls in the duplicated IKBKG/pseudogene region.

clinical.interpretation: Check whether the recurrent IKBKG exon 4-10 deletion sits on the functional IKBKG haplotype (pathogenic) or only on the IKBKGP1 pseudogene (benign). Incontinentia pigmenti is X-linked dominant.
clinical.normal: Intact IKBKG; a deletion confined to the IKBKGP1 pseudogene (common, ~10-12%) is benign.
clinical.carrier: X-linked dominant -- heterozygous females with the gene deletion are typically affected, not silent carriers.
clinical.pathogenic: IKBKG exon 4-10 deletion on the functional gene haplotype -> incontinentia pigmenti.
clinical.caveats: X-linked with male lethality; a gene-level deletion in a viable male suggests mosaicism or an atypical rearrangement.

regions.summary: NCF1 copy-number and pseudogene-aware calls relevant to oxidative burst disease and Williams syndrome region interpretation.

clinical.interpretation: Interpret the count of functional NCF1 copies (GTGT at exon 2) out of the ~6 NCF1-family copies: 2 functional = normal, 1 = carrier, 0 = p47phox-deficient chronic granulomatous disease (recessive).
clinical.pathogenic: 0 functional GTGT copies (all delta-GT) -> p47phox CGD (>97% of p47phox patients).
clinical.caveats: Recessive; NCF1-family copy number varies between people, so judge the functional-copy count relative to total rather than a fixed ratio.

regions.summary: NEB duplicated-region calls relevant to nemaline myopathy.

clinical.interpretation: The NEB triplicate (TRI) region is normally 3 copies per allele (diploid 6). Pathogenicity is per-allele deviation: +/-1 block is benign, but a gain/loss of >=2 blocks per allele on both alleles is recessive-pathogenic. Total CN alone is ambiguous -- inspect the TRI haplotype distribution.
clinical.normal: Total CN 6 (3 per allele); CN 5 or 7 (a single-block change) is a benign polymorphism.
clinical.carrier: One allele with a >=2-block deviation, the other normal.
clinical.pathogenic: Biallelic >=2-block deviation (often a high total CN) -> NEB-related nemaline myopathy.
clinical.caveats: Recessive and per-allele; total CN cannot be classified without allele-level phasing, and TRI CNVs explain only ~10-15% of NEB myopathy.

regions.summary: F8 intron 22 inversion and related structural events in hemophilia A.

clinical.interpretation: Look for the recurrent intron 22 inversion (int22h-1<->int22h-3; a hybrid h1-start/h3-end haplotype) or the intron 1 inversion. Hemophilia A is X-linked recessive.
clinical.normal: Three int22h haplotypes in their expected orientation with no hybrid/inversion breakpoint.
clinical.carrier: Heterozygous female with the inversion = carrier (~30% have FVIII <40% and bleeding risk).
clinical.pathogenic: Intron 22 inversion (~45% of severe hemophilia A) or intron 1 inversion (~2-5%); in a male this means affected (severe).
clinical.caveats: X-linked -- call sex and zygosity carefully; inversions occur only in severe disease, not mild/moderate HA.

regions.summary: CFC1 region calls relevant to heterotaxy and laterality disorders.

clinical.interpretation: Confirm any loss-of-function variant or copy-number change is on the functional CFC1 (not the CFC1B paralog). CFC1 is an uncommon, reduced-penetrance cause of heterotaxy/laterality defects -- treat a finding as supportive evidence.
clinical.normal: Two intact functional CFC1 copies; benign reduced-penetrance polymorphisms (e.g. N21H, R47Q) occur in unaffected people.
clinical.carrier: No clean recessive carrier model; a heterozygous LoF/CNV may be a risk allele transmitted by unaffected parents.
clinical.pathogenic: Loss-of-function variant or CNV of functional CFC1, associated with heterotaxy / complex CHD (supportive, not definitive).
clinical.caveats: Incomplete penetrance and genetic heterogeneity -- correlate with phenotype and other heterotaxy genes.

regions.summary: X-linked opsin array copy-number and haplotype calls relevant to color vision deficiency.

clinical.interpretation: Interpret the OPN1LW/OPN1MW array as structural integrity (locus control region + gene copies) AND the exon-3 haplotype of the expressed copies. Disease arises only when all expressed copies are inactivated.
clinical.normal: One OPN1LW then 1-3 OPN1MW copies (total ~2-4), intact LCR, and a normal exon-3 haplotype on the expressed copies.
clinical.carrier: Females may carry a deleterious haplotype or array SV on one X and be asymptomatic; large arrays (>3 genes) are less stable.
clinical.pathogenic: Blue cone monochromacy when all expressed copies are nonfunctional -- LCR/cluster deletion, p.Cys203Arg, or deleterious exon-3 haplotypes (LIAVA, LVAVA, LIAVS).
clinical.caveats: Allele- and position-dependent -- copy number alone is insufficient; a deleterious haplotype matters only if it is in an expressed copy.

regions.summary: Alpha-globin locus copy-number calls relevant to alpha-thalassemia.

clinical.interpretation: Severity tracks the number of functional alpha-globin genes (normal = 4): 4 normal, 3 silent carrier, 2 alpha-thalassemia trait, 1 HbH disease, 0 Hb Bart hydrops fetalis.
clinical.carrier: 3 (silent carrier) or 2 (alpha-thalassemia trait -- the reproductive carrier state).
clinical.pathogenic: 1 -> HbH disease; 0 -> Hb Bart hydrops fetalis (usually fatal in utero).
clinical.caveats: Copy number cannot distinguish cis vs trans at total 2, and non-deletional variants (e.g. Hb Constant Spring) are missed.

regions.summary: GBA copy-number and recombinant allele calls in the GBA/GBAP1 region.

clinical.interpretation: Paraphase resolves GBA1 from the GBAP1 pseudogene and reports recombinant/fusion alleles (RecNciI, RecTL, RecTL+55) and point variants. Gaucher disease is recessive (biallelic); a single GBA1 variant is a carrier and a low-penetrance Parkinson risk factor.
clinical.normal: Two intact GBA1 copies; pseudogene-only (GBAP1) variants are not disease-causing.
clinical.carrier: One GBA1 pathogenic/recombinant allele -- no Gaucher disease, but elevated Parkinson risk.
clinical.pathogenic: Biallelic GBA1 damaging variants (recombinant/fusion alleles and/or known pathogenic variants e.g. N370S/L444P); recombinant/null alleles tend to be more severe.
clinical.caveats: Allele/variant-dependent, not a copy-number call; a benign GBAP1-internal variant must not be mistaken for a GBA1 recombinant.

regions.summary: CYP11B1/CYP11B2 copy-number and hybrid gene calls relevant to adrenal steroid disorders.

clinical.interpretation: Normal individuals carry distinct CYP11B1 and CYP11B2. A CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric (fusion) allele causes glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism (GRA / familial hyperaldosteronism type 1) and is autosomal dominant -- a single chimera is sufficient.
clinical.normal: Intact, separate CYP11B1 and CYP11B2 with no fusion/chimeric haplotype.
clinical.carrier: Not applicable -- autosomal dominant; a chimera-positive person is affected/at-risk, not a silent carrier.
clinical.pathogenic: A CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric/fusion allele -> GRA/FH-I; confirm biochemically.
clinical.caveats: Phenotype and penetrance depend on the crossover breakpoint; correlate the fusion call with biochemistry.

regions.summary: CFH/CFHR large deletion and duplication calls relevant to complement-mediated disease.

clinical.interpretation: Interpret by which genes are deleted/duplicated AND whether a breakpoint creates a CFH-involving hybrid. CFHR-only changes are mostly risk modifiers; CFH::CFHR hybrids are high-risk for atypical HUS.
clinical.normal: Two intact copies of CFH and of each CFHR gene; a heterozygous CFHR3-CFHR1 deletion is common and on its own is only a modifier.
clinical.carrier: Homozygous CFHR3-CFHR1 deletion predisposes to anti-Factor-H-antibody aHUS but is protective against AMD; CFHR-only rearrangements are moderate-risk.
clinical.pathogenic: CFH-involving rearrangements (CFH::CFHR1 hybrid, reverse CFHR1::CFH, CFH duplication) = high-risk for aHUS.
clinical.caveats: These are risk/modifier findings, not deterministic; the same CFHR3-CFHR1 deletion raises aHUS risk but lowers AMD risk, and only CFH-breakpoint hybrids carry the high-risk signal.

expected_copy_number_note: expected_copy_number is per chromosome copy (haploid): an autosomal or female X-linked region expects twice the value, a male X-linked region once. A [min, max] pair is a normal range. Fields without an expectation are not assessed for a copy-number change.
